prompt:
Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create ONE character or object sprite, rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art: a figure assembled from individually cut pieces of matte colored cardstock and fine-grain craft paper.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.

SUBJECT AND POSE:
An OBJECT: the LEFT half of a CLOSED theatre stage CURTAIN, hanging perfectly straight down, NOT tied back, NO tie-back band, NO rope, NO rod, NO valance. It is a tall panel made of 5 long vertical overlapping paper strips in the SAME reds as the curtain in the reference icon: tomato red (#E0563B), scarlet (#C8402E), deep bean red (#A93B32), alternating, each strip one flat colour, like soft vertical folds. The top edge is straight and flat. The bottom edge is straight with very gently rounded strip ends. The left edge is straight. The right edge (where it meets the other half) is a gently wavy vertical line. Tall and narrow, about twice as tall as wide.

This is an OBJECT, not a character: NO face, NO eyes, NO mouth anywhere on it.

If a reference image is attached, it shows how this character (or this family of objects) is drawn in this exact style: keep the same drawing style, body shapes, face and proportions; take the COLOURS, clothes, markings and POSE from the SUBJECT text above when it says so.

FRAMING:
Tall portrait image. The whole object is visible and centred, filling about 92% of the frame height. Background: a completely flat, uniform, solid magenta (#FF00FF) chroma-key sheet with no texture, no floor, no ground shadow, no extra props, no border. Nothing else in the image.

LIGHTING:
Use soft, diffuse studio-style lighting from the upper-left, mainly to reveal the edges and spacing of stacked paper layers.
Shadows should be short, soft, restrained, and consistent.
They must feel like paper-layer shadows, NOT realistic sunlight shadows cast by natural three-dimensional objects.

OVERALL FEELING:
Warm, tactile, whimsical, handcrafted, elegant, slightly imperfect, sophisticated paper craft, photographed straight from the front. All cast shadows fall toward the LOWER RIGHT (light source at the upper left), short and identical in direction on every piece.

NO text.
NO photorealism.
NO glossy surfaces.
NO realistic 3D modeling.
NO inflated or rounded forms.
NO clay-like volume.
NO gradients.
NO painterly rendering.
NO airbrushed shading.
NO realistic sunlight shadows.
NO deep ambient occlusion.
NO thick beveled edges.
NO plastic appearance.
NO felt or fabric appearance.
NO fur-fibre texture.
NO magenta or hot-pink anywhere inside the subject.

The reference image is our app logo: a paper-art night theatre stage seen through an arched window. Recreate THE SAME PICTURE as a high-resolution, sharp, square image, as faithfully as possible: the SAME composition and proportions, the same red layered paper curtain on the left with its straw-gold tie-back band at the same height, the same cream paper moon hanging on a gold string from the top edge with the same soft warm glow, the same four gold paper stars in the same positions and sizes, the same navy paper sky, the same straw-gold scalloped stage edge and the same orange stage floor below it. Fill the WHOLE square: do NOT draw the arch shape, NO cream background, NO border, NO rounded corners, NO frame. The navy sky continues into the top corners, the curtain continues straight up to the top edge, the orange floor reaches the bottom edge and the side edges. Keep everything at the same place relative to each other; only extend the picture outward so the arch area is fully covered with a little margin. Matte hand-cut cardstock paper with visible fine paper fibres, flat single-colour pieces, short soft warm shadows under each cut edge. NO text, NO gloss, NO gradients inside paper pieces (only the moon glow), NO faces.

The reference image is our paper-art night theatre stage. Recreate THE SAME stage, same framing and scale, as a high-resolution square image, but WITHOUT the moon and WITHOUT its string (the moon is added later as a separate piece): only the navy paper night sky (#1F2A56) with the same small gold paper stars in the same places, plus two more small stars on the left side. Fill the WHOLE square: NO arch shape, NO border, NO frame, NO curtain anywhere (the red curtain of the reference is REMOVED; the sky simply continues where it was). The straw-gold scalloped stage edge and the orange stage floor stay at EXACTLY the same height, size and shape as in the reference and now continue across the FULL width to both side edges. Matte hand-cut cardstock paper with visible fine paper fibres, flat single-colour pieces, short soft warm shadows under each cut edge. NO text, NO gloss, NO gradients, NO faces.

Fill the WHOLE square: NO arch shape, NO border, NO frame, NO curtain anywhere (the red curtain of the reference is REMOVED; the sky simply continues where it was). The straw-gold scalloped stage edge and the orange stage floor stay at EXACTLY the same height, size and shape as in the reference and now continue across the FULL width to both side edges.
